chunks: And from him, from him, from Ibn Abi Najran, from al-Muthanna, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), that he said:

Regarding a foundling who is found, he said: 'She is free (not a slave), she is not bought and she is not sold. And if a slave is born to you from fornication, then keep him or sell him if you wish; he is your slave.'

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the Two Imams (commonly referring to Imam al-Sadiq or Imam al-Baqir in this chain context).
key_terms.زِنًى: Fornication; sexual intercourse outside of marriage.
key_terms.لَقِيطَةٍ: Foundling; a child found alone without known parents.
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٌ: Slave; a person owned by another.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a found child (laqeeṭah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the foundling (laeeṭah) is declared free by default, distinguishing her from slaves who can be traded. The hadith further clarifies the status of a slave born to a master from a concubine (umm walad context), granting the master the discretion to either emancipate or retain her as property. This ruling highlights the flexibility in manumission practices within Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the master's choice in the latter case.
